_note: The leave travel concession, per journey (D-100; rulebook SAL-LTA-001 to -005, -NEW-001; H-8): the lesser of the amount actually incurred on the travel and the fare the Rules admit for its mode, which the taxpayer states; the total never exceeds the assistance received (Sch. III Table Sl. 8(d): "shall in no case exceed the amount of expenses actually incurred"). TY 2026-27, Income-tax Rules, 2026 r.278(1) (pp.1775–1776): "(i) where the journey is performed by air, the amount shall not exceed the fare admissible for the class of travel to which the employee is entitled, by the shortest route …; (ii) … connected by rail … any mode … other than by air, … the air-conditioned first-class rail fare by the shortest route …; (iii) … not connected by rail … (A) where a recognised public transport system exists, … the 1st class or deluxe class fare …; and (B) where no recognised public transport system exists … ₹30 per kilometre" (SAL-LEAVE-TRAVEL-DISTANCE-RATE); not in the new regime, s.202(2)(a)(i). TY 2025-26, Income-tax Rules, 1962 r.2B(1): "(i) … by air, an amount not exceeding the air economy fare of the national carrier by the shortest route …; (ii) … the air-conditioned first class rail fare …; (iii)(A) … the 1st class or deluxe class fare …; (B) … an amount equivalent to the air-conditioned first class rail fare, for the distance of the journey by the shortest route, as if the journey had been performed by rail"; excluded in the new regime by s.115BAC(2)(i) (Finance Act, 2023 s.52: "clause (5) or clause (13A) … of section 10"). The children limit (r.278(5)–(6); SAL-LTA-CHILD-001) is not modelled (Appendix F).
